competitor_summaries.name: Bar-B-Q Tonight
competitor_summaries.positioning_summary: Long-established, heavily positions on brand legacy and being a Lahore institution -- messaging leans on years in business and being a known name rather than any specific menu detail.

competitor_summaries.name: Butt Karahi
competitor_summaries.positioning_summary: Positions on portion size and value, with a straightforward, no-frills menu presentation -- similar territory to FirePit's own stated USP.

cross_competitor_patterns: Both established competitors lean on trust/legacy signals (years in business, branch count) rather than describing what makes the food itself distinct.
Neither makes a specific claim about grilling method, marinade, or ingredient sourcing -- 'authentic charcoal grilling' is not a claim either of them visibly makes.
Both are positioned for dine-in/family outings first, with delivery treated as secondary.

differentiation_angles.angle: Make 'authentic charcoal grilling with bold marinades' an explicit, visible claim rather than assumed.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Neither competitor states their grilling method or marinade approach anywhere visible -- as a new entrant, a specific, stated claim is more memorable than legacy/trust messaging you can't yet compete on.

differentiation_angles.angle: Lead with delivery-first, group-occasion framing (match nights, iftar) rather than positioning as a dine-in destination.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Both established players are dine-in-first; competing there directly means competing on legacy FirePit doesn't have yet. Group-delivery occasions are comparatively open ground.

differentiation_angles.angle: Use specific, named signature items (e.g. a distinctly branded platter) rather than a generic BBQ menu list.
differentiation_angles.reasoning: Both competitors present fairly generic, undifferentiated menu listings -- a few named, ownable dishes could stand out precisely because the category default is genericness.

caveat: Based on a light read of each competitor's own homepage/profile text, not a full market study -- informed context for your own judgment, not a verdict.
